program:
:- prefix(ex, 'https://example.org/1428/').
ex:ans(X, D) :- X is 0, D is 5 / 0.
?- ex:ans(X, D).

provenance.derivation: 5 / 0: exact rational division by the zero rational (0/1) is undefined -- a declared math:ZeroDivisor domain error, never a silently-computed value (e.g. never 0 and never an unbounded/infinite surface). `X` is an unused dummy arg (`X is 0`) so the goal atom is arity >= 2, keeping the query on the binary backward path (which actually evaluates the builtin) rather than the arity-generic path (which refuses ANY builtin unconditionally, positive-Datalog-only) -- see the corpus README's arity note; this is what makes the refusal below trace to the REAL zero-divisor condition rather than the arity-routing gap.
provenance.note: independently derived; never hand-edited to match the native engine. OBSERVABILITY CAVEAT: the public dispatch_query surface collapses every domain gap to the same opaque 'Arithmetic' refusal message -- see quantity_add_dimension_mismatch.json's note for the full explanation. This case only proves the engine refuses rather than divides by zero; it cannot independently confirm the refusal was specifically tagged ZeroDivisor internally.
